name: Lemuel
title: The Wise King
summary: King Lemuel is a figure mentioned in Proverbs chapter 31, known for the wise words his mother taught him. His identity is debated—some scholars believe he may be Solomon under another name, while others regard him as an unknown Arab or non-Israelite king. His most significant contribution to the Bible is the famous hymn about the capable woman in Proverbs 31.

keyEvents.title: Mother's Exhortation on Kingship
keyEvents.description: King Lemuel's mother gave him wise counsel on how a king should live, including warnings against women and wine.

keyEvents.title: Warnings Against Wine and Strong Drink
keyEvents.description: Lemuel's mother warned him against drinking wine and strong drink, as this can lead kings to forget the laws and oppress the poor.

keyEvents.title: Defense of the Weak and Justice
keyEvents.description: Lemuel was urged to speak up for those who cannot speak and defend the rights of all helpless people, as well as to judge fairly and uphold the cause of the poor and needy.

keyEvents.title: Hymn of the Capable Woman
keyEvents.description: Proverbs 31:10-31 contains the famous acrostic hymn about the capable woman, traditionally attributed to the teaching of Lemuel's mother.
